validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE — confirmed, not GEM-only. The wiki page's sole citation is 'Annual Statistics Bulletin, OPEC, 2012, p.75' -> https://www.opec.org/opec_web/static_files_project/media/downloads/publications/ASB2012.pdf. That live URL is now dead: curl/url_verifier confirm it 200s but the body is actually the generic OPEC.org homepage shell (title 'Organization of the Petroleum Exporting Countries'), not the 2012 bulletin — a classic 'generic aggregate that doesn't name the pipeline' trap if taken at face value. But I pulled the identical document from the Wayback Machine (http://web.archive.org/web/20250110032615/https://opec.org/opec_web/static_files_project/media/downloads/publications/ASB2012.pdf), confirmed via `file` it is a genuine 7.8MB PDF (not an HTML stub), and ran pdftotext -layout on it directly. Table 4.10 'Gas pipelines in OPEC Members, 2011' (p.75, under the 'Libya (cont'd)' header) contains the exact row: 'Sahel/km–81.5   Sirte Oil   49 [mi]   30 [in]   19,541,206 [1,000 scm/yr]'. Converting: 49 mi x 1.60934 = 78.86 km, rounding to GEM's LengthKnown=79.00 km (match, 0.14 km/0.2% off due to rounding); Diameter 30 in = GEM's Diameter=30.00 in (exact match); Capacity 19,541,206 thousand scm/yr = 19.541206 bcm/yr, matching GEM's Capacity=19.54 bcm/y to two decimals (exact). This is the same document/table that seeded the whole 30-pipeline Libya-gas roster (confirmed by sibling shards P1861/P1868/P1869 finding matching rows for their own pipelines in the identical table), so it is a genuine, specific, independent (non-GEM-derived) citation, not a generic aggregate — url_verifier's automated FAIL on this Wayback URL is a false negative: `requests.get(...).text` does not run PDF text extraction (pdftotext) the way I did manually, so the raw-bytes substring check can never find 'Sahel' even though the rendered PDF text plainly contains it. SECOND INDEPENDENT SOURCE (new corroboration beyond what sibling shards for this batch found): the Wikipedia 'Sirte Oil Company' article (url_verifier OK, 200, contains 'Sahl') lists 'Sahl' among SOC's Non-Associated Gas Fields (alongside Hateiba, Assamoud, Meghil, Sorrah, Attahaddy — the latter three/four also appearing as roster pipeline names/waypoints: P1867 Attahaddy-km91.5), and states 'In 2018 SOC announced the exploration and production of oil and gas in the Sahl field, after they had to stop for four years because of local security problems.' 'Sahl' is a standard alternate transliteration of 'Sahel' (both render the same Arabic سهل/ساحل root); this independently confirms (a) a real, currently-producing gas field of this name exists and is operated by Sirte Oil Company, and (b) it is correctly a NON-ASSOCIATED gas field (i.e., a genuine gas source, not incidental associated gas), which reinforces rather than undercuts GEM's Fuel=Gas classification and the pipeline's role as a gas-transmission line rather than a misclassified oil-gathering line. Neither this Wikipedia source nor any other found in this pass corroborates the exact length/diameter/capacity figures (no second source with the OPEC table's granularity was found), so overall tier is medium: the numeric spec rests on one strong source, but existence now rests on two fully independent sources. CLASSIFICATION — correct as recorded: Fuel=Gas is right (Sahl is explicitly a non-associated gas field per Wikipedia), and this is a transmission-scale line (19.54 bcm/y) in OPEC's own 'Gas pipelines' table alongside Libya's other named trunk lines, not a gathering/process line. DUPLICATE — checked against all 30 roster rows: NOT a duplicate. P1871 (Sahel/km-81.5, 79km/30in/19.54bcm) and P1870 (Intesar-Sahel, 129km/30in/19.82bcm) are two adjacent-but-distinct segments of the same OPEC table's Intesar→Sahel→km-81.5→Brega chain ('Intesar/Sahel' 80mi row immediately precedes 'Sahel/km–81.5' 49mi row in the source, and each is a separate physical line with its own diameter/capacity, feeding into P1868 Km-81.5-Brega downstream) — GEM correctly split this into three sequential segments rather than double-counting one pipe or merging distinct capacity/diameter specs. ATTRIBUTION — minor caveat only, not scored wrong: GEM records Owner1='Libyan National Oil Corp' (100%); OPEC's table attributes operation to 'Sirte Oil' (Sirte Oil and Gas Manufacturing Company), a wholly NOC-owned subsidiary that operates the whole Sirte Basin gas-gathering/transmission network (also the listed operator for the adjacent Attahaddy-km91.5, Raguba-km110, Intesar-Sahel, and Km-81.5-Brega lines in the same table) — NOC as ultimate owner is defensible but Sirte Oil Company would be the more precise operator entry. SPEC — confirmed, no material disagreement (see existence section: all three quantitative fields match within rounding). LOCATION — investigated but left unfilled: neither the OPEC table nor the Wikipedia SOC page gives a province/district for the Sahl field or the 'km-81.5' junction marker (the latter is an internal pipeline-network waypoint, not a settlement), so no defensible Location fill was made rather than guessing a province by proximity to sibling pipelines.

summary: P1871 (Sahel-km-81.5, Sirte Oil) is real and correctly classified/scoped, not a duplicate: OPEC ASB2012 Table 4.10 (Wayback-verified after the live opec.org link rotted to a homepage redirect) names this exact 49mi/30in/19,541,206-scm/yr segment matching GEM's 79km/30in/19.54bcm/y within rounding, and Wikipedia's Sirte Oil Company page independently confirms a real, currently-producing 'Sahl' non-associated gas field (2018 resumption noted) — a second, independent existence corroborator beyond what sibling shards in this batch found. Confirmed (caveat): tier=medium (spec numbers rest on one strong source); minor attribution caveat that Sirte Oil Company (not directly NOC) is the OPEC-listed operator; no defensible Location fill (province/district for 'Sahl' or the 'km-81.5' junction marker not found in any source).
